item.title: Black Friday: Where in Europe are shoppers the gloomiest?
item.description: As Black Friday deals hit Europe, new European Commission data show consumer confidence ranging from cautious optimism in Malta and near-neutral sentiment in Spain to deep gloom in Greece, while Italians cut back sharply on plans for big purchases.

item.title: Trump tariffs brought EU and Indonesia closer on trade, minister tells Euronews
item.description: US tariffs brought the EU and Indonesia closer, Indonesia's Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto said in an exclusive interview with Euronews. After a decade of talks, the two sides signed a deal last week, and the minister expects it to lift trade by 50% in three years.

item.title: 'Colourful and complicated': New London Museum promises to show city in all its glory
item.description: After a a decade-long transformation costing more than €500 million, London Museum reopens its doors this weekend at the former Victorian General Market at Smithfield and it's billing itself as the world's largest city museum.

item.title: A green valley with a circular twist: Austria´s shapes the sustainable tech of tomorrow
item.description: Austria´s Green Tech Valley Cluster hosts 300 companies — including 20 global tech leaders — shaping the innovative and circular technologies of the future. They are developing solutions in sectors like hydropower, solar thermal, wind, recycling, batteries or electro-mobility — all made in Europe.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan reopen key border crossing for up to 100,000 travellers a day
item.description: The reopening comes as the EU seeks stronger transport and trade links with Central Asia. The upgraded checkpoint could also ease pressure on regional freight routes and support cross-border tourism.

item.title: EU budget summit collapses as row over money exposes clash over Europe's strategic tasks
item.description: The EU summit on the Union's common budget for 2028-2034 has initially failed. Some want to protect established spending, others to cut costs and mainly finance new strategic tasks, warns foreign policy expert Alexander Wolf of the Hanns Seidel Foundation in Berlin.

item.title: ‘Live and ongoing’ cyber incident takes down UK Department for Work and Pensions online services
item.description: The UK government department took the decision to take down the services as a precaution after it detected a cyber incident affecting its systems.

item.title: Meet Eba, the 11-year-old poop-sniffing dog helping to protect endangered orcas
item.description: Unlike most pooches, Eba spends her days on a boat - assisting scientists in the fight to save dwindling killer whale populations.

item.title: North Korea halts Russia military aid over Seoul row, Kyiv says
item.description: Ukraine's military intelligence said Kim Jong-un personally ordered the suspension after Russia's deputy foreign minister said it would help ease tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang.

item.title: No burqas at school and fewer foreign pupils: Italy passes controversial education law
item.description: The school decree, which includes new rules on digital transition, was finally approved in the Chamber on Thursday. During the vote, opposition MPs displayed signs saying "At school no one is a foreigner".

item.title: France's government faces mounting pressure from both sides of the barricades
item.description: Exhausted by weeks of street protests, French police officers are demanding better pay, more resources and greater protection. Meanwhile, students and trade unions are determined to maintain their mobilisation, despite what they deem as a strategy of repression aimed at stifling the movement.

item.title: EU budget row: Macron accuses Le Pen of 'strange arrogance'
item.description: The RN presidential candidate accuses the European Commission of seeking to "rush" adoption of the next EU budget before the 2027 French election.

item.title: Son of Myanmar's Suu Kyi 'relieved' by first call in five years, questions military's motives
item.description: Speaking to Euronews’ The World Conversation, Kim Aris described his relief at hearing his mother’s voice after five years, called for tougher sanctions enforcement and defended her record on the Rohingya genocide ruling.

item.title: Video captures king tide sweeping man and dog into the sea
item.description: A man and his dog were swept into the surf by a powerful incoming wave at Cannon Beach, Oregon, after he had earlier been warned by police about the dangers of King Tides. Both managed to escape the water without injury.

item.title: A travel guide to Ljubljana – a 2027 European Capital of Tourism
item.description: Named one of the European Capitals of Tourism for 2027, Ljubljana offers travellers riverside cafés, historic landmarks and traditional cuisine. Here’s why you should visit the Slovenian capital.

item.title: Portugal's parliament orders public TV to air bullfights again, sparking 86,000-name petition
item.description: After six years away, bullfights are set to return to RTP programming in 2027, via a Chega proposal, sparking controversy and a petition with over 86,000 signatures.

item.title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth' - Fincher with fries?
item.description: Nostalgia and nihilism collide in David Fincher's gritty but edgeless follow-up to Quentin Tarantino's 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood'.

item.title: Marseille stadium violence escalates into diplomatic affair between France and Bulgaria
item.description: Clashes between Marseille and Bulgarian fans broke out on Thursday evening before the Europa League match OM–Levski Sofia; eleven Bulgarians were injured, five hospitalised.

item.title: Does Europe have a cybersecurity problem? | Password
item.description: According to experts, the cybersecurity incidents Europe experienced in November should not come as a surprise. But how much do we know about these attacks? And what can Europe do to improve its cybersecurity?

item.title: Feijóo vows to quit if he loses Spanish election and dares Sánchez to do the same
item.description: Feijóo dared Sánchez to give up his seat and his legal protection if he loses. The prime minister declined.

item.title: Spain’s conservative and far-right parties likely to ‘secure a majority’ in Sunday’s election, expert says
item.description: Javier Martínez-Cantó, political scientist at the Institute of Public Goods and Policies (IPP–CSIC), believes corruption scandals "have been hindering the popularity" of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez as he tries to stay in power ahead of Sunday's snap elections.

item.title: A travel guide to Calvià – a 2027 European Capital of Tourism
item.description: Recognised as one of the 2027 European Capitals of Tourism, Calvià is an ideal destination for travellers looking for more than sun and sand. Here’s what you can discover.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 27th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 27th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: NATO jets scrambled after drone briefly enters Latvian airspace
item.description: Latvia's army hasn't said where the drone came from, and it warns more incursions are likely.

item.title: German sofware giant SAP weighs at least 10,000 job cuts amid AI shift, reports say
item.description: If confirmed, the cuts could affect about 9% of the company's global workforce. SAP's shares in Frankfurt were down on Friday morning.

item.title: New ECB chief should prioritise inflation, economist says
item.description: Spanish economist Pablo Hernández de Cos has been named as the next president of the European Central Bank, replacing Christine Lagarde from February 2027.

item.title: Iran denies responsibility for Kuwait drone strike that killed two Italians
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the accusations baseless and the incident "suspicious" and offered to cooperate on a joint investigation. Kuwait called it "a heinous Iranian aggression". Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar and the UAE condemned the attack.

item.title: Video shows Levski fan caught giving Nazi salute before Marseille match
item.description: Violent clashes marred Marseille’s Europa League win over Levski Sofia, with a filmed Nazi salute, flares, injuries and condemnation from both presidents.

item.title: Trump’s latest tariffs attempt to revive old policy, trade expert says
item.description: Hosuk Lee-Makiyama, a Brussels-based trade economist, told Euronews new US tariffs were an attempt to bring back earlier tariffs under a different law.

item.title: Footage shows skidding truck end up hanging between highway ramps
item.description: A container truck lost control on in Toledo, Ohio, skidding across a gap between two elevated roadways and becoming stranded over the edge.

item.title: France's inflation slows to 2.9% in November as energy prices fall
item.description: Consumer prices fell by 0.7% in November 2026, after rising by 0.4% in October, according to the latest figures from Insee, published this Friday.

item.title: What the ECB’s new leadership could mean for interest rates
item.description: Pablo Hernández de Cos is set to succeed Christine Lagarde with eurozone inflation at twice the ECB’s target. Analysts expect broad policy continuity, but say he could take a more direct role in shaping interest-rate decisions.

item.title: Estonia prepares to close all five road border crossings with Russia
item.description: Long queues have formed at Estonia's border with Russia ahead of its planned closure on 1 December. The decision, prompted by security concerns, threatens to separate families and disrupt local businesses.

item.title: Shanghai named the world's best shopping city – and Europe has just six entries in the top 20
item.description: Europe may be home to three of the world’s fashion capitals, but it has just six cities in Time Out’s top 20 shopping destinations ranking, with only London and Copenhagen making the top 10.

item.title: Kim Jong Un watches Russian performers in Pyongyang
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has attended a performance by a Russian artistic troupe in Pyongyang, alongside his wife Ri Sol Ju and Russian Natural Resources Minister Alexander Kozlov.

item.title: Germany and Austria push for European ownership of TikTok
item.description: The two countries want TikTok’s European business and key technology, including its recommendation algorithm, to come under European control, arguing that regulation alone cannot address security concerns.

item.title: Thanksgiving turkeys fall from the sky for families in remote Alaska
item.description: Two friends in Alaska take to the skies each year to deliver Thanksgiving turkeys to families living in isolated wilderness communities, some completely off the grid and around 50 miles from the nearest road.

item.title: Denmark arrests teenager over data breach affecting 11,000 people
item.description: An 18-year-old has been detained over the latest breach of Denmark’s national civil registry, two months after a separate cyberattack exposed data linked to 8.8 million people.

item.title: Russia: Moscow's iconic Soviet-era expo park opens its 20,000-square-metre outdoor ice rink
item.description: Moscow's iconic VDNKh exhibition park has opened its vast outdoor ice rink for the winter season on Thursday 26 November 2026, welcoming skaters to 20,000 square metres of ice winding around the complex's landmark Soviet-era fountains.

item.title: The art of no deal: An EU summit of spectacular dysfunction
item.description: Good morning. Leo Cendrowicz here with your Friday newsletter. They rush in, elbow each other out of the way, squabble over the price and emerge with precious little to show for it. But enough about Black Friday - we also have an angry EU summit to report on…

item.title: Italian brand Armani to expand its luxury hotel empire in Egypt and Saudi Arabia
item.description: The Italian fashion house is expanding beyond its existing hotels in Dubai and Milan, with a new Red Sea resort planned for 2030 and a Riyadh opening expected next year.

item.title: Half of new HIV diagnoses in Greece are made late, early data shows
item.description: The number of new HIV diagnoses has fallen over the past year, but late diagnoses remain a challenge in Greece.

item.title: Europe Today: EU leaders unable to find an agreement on EU's budget
item.description: The European Union’s 27 leaders met in Brussels yesterday with the aim of trying to find common ground on finalising the bloc’s budget. But red lines seemed to have deepened between the budget’s main opposing camps, we debrief the summit with our correspondents Angela Skujins and Sasha Vakulina.

item.title: Clashes erupt at Besiktas Europa League match against Israeli club
item.description: Besiktas supporters clashed with police in Batumi during a Europa League match against Israeli club Hapoel Beer-Sheva, with fans chanting and officers pursuing supporters outside the stadium.

item.title: Germany's IG Metall reaches pay deal amid industrial crisis
item.description: A pay deal that could cover 3.7 million workers across Germany raises wages in two stages and lets struggling manufacturers seek labour cost savings in return for binding pledges to invest and protect jobs in Germany.

item.title: Why European households are rushing to buy solar panels ahead of a dark, cold winter
item.description: Changes to solar incentives and long installation processes mean European homeowners could benefit from planning now.

item.title: Mixing drugs is now the norm, EU drugs agency warns
item.description: Most drug-related ER visits in a new survey involved people who had taken more than one drug or mixed drugs with alcohol.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 27th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: These are Europe’s best attractions for families to visit in 2027, according to travellers
item.description: Trip.com has ranked Europe’s best family-friendly attractions for 2027, with Disneyland Paris at number one and London landmarks dominating the top 10.

item.title: New Zealand election: newcomer centrist party to decide as Luxon scrambles for a majority
item.description: The final count showed more support for minor parties on the ideological flanks than before. A total of 2.8 million votes were cast.
